deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no derivations, formulas or computations. It is a sequence of aphorisms and methodological remarks from Hilbert's notebook. The entries continue the previous page's maxims on mathematical work and the axiomatic method.

(1) Physicists who cannot get a result blame matter for the difficulties. Philosophers say an unsolved problem exceeds the limits of reason ('Transcendenz'). Only the mathematician knows the failure is always his own stupidity; for him there is no 'ignorabimus'. He can plead neither the veto of material nor of spiritual forces. This is the private, blunter form of the solvability credo Hilbert announced publicly in Paris in 1900 ('in der Mathematik giebt es kein Ignorabimus') and repeated in Königsberg in 1930 ('Wir müssen wissen, wir werden wissen'). It is aimed at Du Bois-Reymond's 'Ignoramus et ignorabimus' of 1872/1880.

(2) Most theorems of mathematics have not yet been discovered, 'so get to it!' The same maxim recurs on the next page.

(3) It is wrong to say nature is everywhere inexact and phenomena only approximately valid. Rather, our understanding grasps only the exact perfectly; instead of blaming nature one should praise the understanding. Where the physicist says a law holds only approximately, the mathematician should 'prepare out' the rigorous limit process. This is an idealization-by-limits programme, consistent with Hilbert's later treatment of physical laws as limiting idealizations in his axiomatic physics lectures.

(4) Mathematicians can only create schemata, logical frameworks ('logische Fachwerke'). The same schema often fits quite different groups of phenomena. His examples:
- point and line geometry, i.e. projective duality / Plücker line geometry, where one formal theory has two interpretations;
- potential theory applied to electricity, magnetism, heat, etc.
This is the 'one formalism, many models' view that underlies the Grundlagen der Geometrie (1899) and the Frege correspondence ('tables, chairs, beer mugs').

(5) The axiomatic route suits both the beginner and the advanced researcher. The researcher must prove the (in)dependence and consistency of the axioms; the beginner simply accepts them as facts. The old mathematicians differ from today's beginner only in that they accepted dependence and consistency unconsciously, the beginner consciously. The axiomatic way is the long-sought 'royal road' in mathematics, alluding to Euclid's 'there is no royal road to geometry'. Hilbert says he will show it is certainly a royal road to mathematical physics, a programmatic link to Problem 6 of 1900 and his Göttingen lectures on the axiomatization of physics (c. 1905 onward).
errors: No mathematical errors are possible since there are no derivations.

'Abhängigkeit' (both occurrences) is almost certainly meant as or abbreviates '(Un)abhängigkeit'. The standard metatheoretic tasks in Hilbert's axiomatics are independence and consistency (Unabhängigkeit und Widerspruchsfreiheit/-losigkeit). It is a slip or abbreviation, not a substantive claim.

The sentence 'Der axiomatische Weg ist zugleich für den Anfänger wie für den Forscher ...' lacks a predicate (e.g. 'der richtige/geeignete'). It is a grammatical ellipsis typical of notebook jottings.

results.what: Mathematical solvability credo: for the mathematician there is no 'ignorabimus'; failure is always due to one's own limitation, not matter or the limits of reason
results.modern_name: Hilbert's 'no ignorabimus' / solvability axiom (Lösbarkeit jedes mathematischen Problems)
results.usually_credited_to: David Hilbert (Paris ICM address 1900; Königsberg address 1930), reacting to Emil du Bois-Reymond (1872)

results.what: Approximate physical laws should be replaced by rigorous limit processes; exactness is a feature of understanding, not a defect of nature
results.modern_name: Idealization via limits / rigorous foundations of mathematical physics
results.usually_credited_to: General 19th-c. view; associated with Hilbert's axiomatization of physics programme (Problem 6, 1900; lectures 1905ff.)

results.what: Mathematics produces formal schemata ('logische Fachwerke') admitting multiple interpretations (point vs. line geometry; potential theory for electricity, magnetism, heat)
results.modern_name: Formal axiomatics / multiple models of one theory (structural view)
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert (Grundlagen der Geometrie 1899; Frege correspondence 1899-1900); antecedents in Plücker/Gergonne duality and Maxwell's analogies

results.what: The axiomatic method as the 'royal road' to mathematics and to mathematical physics; the researcher must prove independence and consistency of axioms
results.modern_name: Axiomatic method; metatheory of independence and consistency

deep.surprise_reason: These are well-known Hilbertian themes in private aphoristic form: no ignorabimus, formal schemata with multiple interpretations, the axiomatic method for physics, independence and consistency. They are mildly interesting as early notebook formulations, e.g. the blunt 'Dummheit' version of the ignorabimus credo and the explicit 'royal road to mathematical physics' claim. Nothing is mathematically new or unexpected.
transcription_corrections: Line 9: the struck-out opening is two deleted words, 'Die' and a second word read as 'aber(t)'. It may be the beginning of 'Die allermeisten', partly cancelled, rather than 'Die aber'. The surviving text reads 'meisten Theoreme in der Mathematik sind noch nicht entdeckt'.
'Wir Mathematiker': the image shows an initial false start of 'Mathematiker' struck through and rewritten, so the text should read 'Wir [-Math-] Mathematiker'.
'Potentialtheorie auf. Elektr.' is more likely 'Potentialtheorie anf.'. This is possibly an abbreviation of 'angewandt auf', or simply 'auf', followed by 'Elektr., Magnet., Wärme etc.'.
'Punkt – Liniengeometrie' = point geometry and line geometry (duality), likely intended as 'Punkt- u. Liniengeometrie'.
'das veto der materielle' should be read 'der materiellen' (noch der geistigen Kräfte).
'die Beweise[?]': the word before 'd.h.' is uncertain and may be 'Resultate' or similar. In either case it is glossed by 'd.h. die Abhängigkeit u. Widerspruchslosigkeit'.
'Abhängigkeit' / 'Abhängigk.' is written thus in both places, though (Un)abhängigkeit is clearly the intended concept.
'der [-?-] lange vergeblich gesuchte Königsweg': there is a small struck mark before 'lange'.
'[-Er-] Ich will zeigen': the struck word is a short form, possibly 'Er' or 'Es'.
